framing_caveat: The IMF reports absolute economy-wide employment shares (77% of Singapore workers highly exposed); this model's exposure is percentile-ranked within 562 SG occupations and cannot reproduce absolute shares by construction. Only the employment-weighted complementarity split among the most-exposed occupations and its direction are comparable. This is a convergent-directional check, not occupation-level validation.

imf_targets.label: IMF SIP/2024/040 — Impact of AI on Singapore's Labor Market (Khan)
imf_targets.framing: IMF reports absolute economy-wide employment shares using the Cazzaniga et al. (2024) exposure x complementarity framework. This repo's exposure is percentile-ranked within 562 Singapore occupations, so absolute shares are not comparable; only the occupational pattern and the complementarity split direction are.

complementarity_cut.note: High complementarity = theta at or above the cross-occupation median.

exposure_mass_diagnostic.note: Continuous secondary diagnostic only — not comparable to IMF share targets.

verdicts: Top half of exposure distribution: employment-weighted complementarity split among exposed workers is 28:31.1 high:low (ratio 0.9) vs IMF ~39:38 (ratio 1.03) — the model is less optimistic on complementarity than the IMF benchmark at this cut.

Top quartile of exposure distribution: employment-weighted complementarity split among exposed workers is 10.8:22.8 high:low (ratio 0.47) vs IMF ~39:38 (ratio 1.03) — the model is less optimistic on complementarity than the IMF benchmark at this cut.
At least one cut diverges meaningfully from the IMF split — disclosed as a candidate recalibration signal, not hidden.
caveats: Employment weights are estimated per-occupation figures derived from published sub-major totals, not official per-occupation headcounts.
The theta median split is a coarse two-way complementarity classification; the IMF uses the Cazzaniga et al. (2024) framework with different thresholds.
Exposure cuts at the top half and top quartile bracket the ambiguity of "highly exposed" against a percentile-internal measure.
This check is a Singapore macro benchmark; the MOM AI-adoption survey (April 2026) remains adoption/context evidence, and the BLS slope specification remains the occupation-level external check.
